newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond yield curve steepens again.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond yield curve steepens again.

text.p: The Australian bond yield curve extended last week's steepening trend amid hopes of an early loosening in monetary policy and as the prospect of fresh supply weighed on the long-end of the market.
Traders said there was some concern over the amount on offer in a new line of September 2009 stock to be tendered on Tuesday, making-up A$600 million of the total A$800 million tender size.

There was also talk of fresh samurai dual-currency bond issuance in the foreign exchange market, which would have bolstered the short-end of curve due to swap-related activity. The three/10-year bond futures spread has now put on some 10 basis points since last Thursday's release the August quarter wages report, which enhanced hopes of an early reduction in official interest rates, possibily as early as next week.

Meanwhile, the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread egded out slightly, continuing a widening trend after touching its lowest level in over two years at around 80 basis points in the aftermath of last week's wages report.
However, spreads to Canadian debt narrowed again as minor profit-taking there was exaggerated in a fairly illiquid market on Friday.
The New Zealand market was closed for a local holiday.
